stories.title: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October, unemployment rises to 6.7%
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported that the Canadian economy shed 4,700 jobs in October 2026, while the unemployment rate increased to 6.7% from 6.5% in September. The loss follows large back‑to‑back job cuts in August and September that together removed more than 100,000 positions. Economists surveyed before the release had expected a gain of about 13,600 jobs for October.
stories.why: The higher unemployment rate signals a weakening labour market.

stories.title: EU launches fraud probe into Spanish rail authorities after deadly high‑speed crash
stories.summary: European Union prosecutors have opened a fraud investigation into possible misuse of EU funds for upgrading Spain’s high‑speed rail network after the 28 October Madrid‑Seville crash that killed 69 people. The inquiry is focused on the rail infrastructure authority Adif and the safety agency AESF. It follows a similar EU fraud probe after a January crash on the same line that killed 46 people.
stories.why: It highlights concerns over how EU funding is used and the oversight of railway safety.

stories.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion, valuation $1.25 trillion
stories.summary: OpenAI has reportedly secured $11 billion in a funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The round is still open and Bloomberg expects it could close in the coming weeks with total commitments around $20 billion, below the earlier September target of $30 billion. TechCrunch has asked OpenAI for comment and is awaiting a response.
stories.why: The influx of capital and trillion‑plus valuation underscore strong investor confidence in generative‑AI and may shift competitive dynamics in the sector.

stories.title: Google buys unfinished Wyoming data center project from Crusoe
stories.summary: Denver‑based data center developer Crusoe confirmed it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. The project, announced last year with Blackstone‑backed Tallgrass and planned to eventually reach 10 GW of power capacity, faced cost and timeline concerns under Crusoe’s management. Google did not disclose the purchase price but announced a $17 billion investment to develop the campus.
stories.why: The deal highlights the difficulty independent developers have delivering large‑scale data center projects on time and within budget.
